topics.title: Overview, Objectives & Key Definitions
topics.concept:
Unit Overview

A differential equation relates a function to its derivative(s). This unit is about modeling change and recovering a function from its rate. You will interpret and build models, visualize solution behavior with slope fields, verify solutions, and solve the one algebraic type AP AB requires — separable equations — including initial-value problems and the important applications of exponential growth/decay and logistic growth.

Scope note. AP Calculus AB covers separable first-order equations, slope fields, and growth/decay/logistic models. It does not require integrating factors, homogeneous or second-order equations (those are JEE / Class-12 topics). This study guide and its question bank are scoped to AP AB.

Big picture: Separate the variables, integrate both sides, then use an initial condition to pin down the constant.

Learning Objectives

  • Interpret and build differential-equation models from a verbal description.
  • Verify whether a given function solves a differential equation.
  • Sketch and read slope fields; match a slope field to its equation.
  • Solve separable equations and initial-value problems.
  • Model and analyze exponential growth and decay (including half-life / doubling time).
  • Understand the logistic model and its carrying capacity.

Prerequisite Concepts

  • Antiderivatives and u-substitution (Unit 6).
  • Properties of e^x and ln.
  • Interpreting derivatives as rates (Unit 4).

Key Definitions

  • Differential equation: an equation involving a function and its derivative(s).
  • General solution: a family of solutions containing an arbitrary constant C.
  • Particular solution: a specific solution determined by an initial condition.
  • Slope field (direction field): a grid of short segments whose slopes equal dy/dx at each point, suggesting solution curves.
  • Equilibrium solution: a constant solution where dy/dx = 0.
  • Carrying capacity (M): the limiting value a logistic population approaches.

quiz.q: A population grows at a rate proportional to its size. Which differential equation models this?
quiz.explanation: "Rate proportional to size" means the derivative dP/dt is a constant k times P, giving dP/dt = kP.

quiz.q: To verify that a function is a solution of a differential equation, you should:
options: substitute the function and its derivatives into the equation and check it holds
quiz.explanation: A function is a solution if substituting it (and its derivatives) into the differential equation produces a true statement.

quiz.q: The first step in solving a separable differential equation dy/dx = g(x)h(y) is to:
options: separate variables so all y-terms are with dy and all x-terms with dx
quiz.explanation: Separation of variables rearranges the equation to (1/h(y)) dy = g(x) dx, then both sides are integrated.

quiz.q: The general solution of the exponential growth equation dy/dt = ky is:
quiz.explanation: The exponential model dy/dt = ky has solution y = y0 e^(kt), where y0 is the initial amount.

quiz.q: A differential equation is an equation that relates a function to:
options: one or more of its derivatives
quiz.explanation: A differential equation involves an unknown function together with one or more of its derivatives.

topics.title: Important Theorems & Formulas
topics.concept:
Important Models & Results

Exponential model: dy/dt = k y ⟹ y = y₀ e^(kt) (growth if k > 0, decay if k < 0).

  • Half-life h: from e^(kh) = 1/2, k = −(ln 2)/h.
  • Doubling time d: from e^(kd) = 2, k = (ln 2)/d.

Logistic model: dP/dt = k P (1 − P/M).

  • Equilibria: P = 0 and P = M.
  • Growth is fastest at P = M/2 (the solution curve's inflection point).
  • As t → ∞, P → M.

Newton's Law of Cooling: dT/dt = k(T − A) (A = ambient temperature; equilibrium T = A).

Method: Separation of Variables

To solve dy/dx = g(x) h(y):

  1. Separate: dy / h(y) = g(x) dx.
  2. Integrate both sides (one + C suffices).
  3. Solve for y if possible.
  4. Apply the initial condition to find C (particular solution).

quiz.q: A curve has the property that the slope of the tangent at any point is twice the slope of the line joining that point to the origin. The differential equation is:
quiz.explanation: The slope of the line to the origin is y/x. Twice this is 2y/x, so dy/dx = 2y/x. (Adapted from the GrowQR JEE bank; its solution is the parabola family y = Cx^2.)

quiz.q: Newton's Law of Cooling says an object's temperature changes at a rate proportional to the difference between the object's temperature T and the ambient temperature A. The model is:
quiz.explanation: The rate of temperature change is proportional to the temperature difference (T - A), giving dT/dt = k(T - A).

quiz.q: Verify: is y = e^(2x) a solution of dy/dx = 2y?
quiz.explanation: If y = e^(2x), then dy/dx = 2e^(2x). Since 2y = 2e^(2x), the equation dy/dx = 2y holds for all x.

quiz.q: Is y = sin(x) a solution of the differential equation y'' + y = 0?
options: Yes, since y'' = -sin(x) and y'' + y = 0
quiz.explanation: y = sin(x) gives y'' = -sin(x). Then y'' + y = -sin(x) + sin(x) = 0, so it is a solution.

quiz.q: For the slope field of dy/dx = x, along the vertical line x = 2 all the slope segments have slope:
quiz.explanation: Since dy/dx = x depends only on x, at x = 2 every segment (for all y) has slope 2.

topics.title: Concept Explanations & Solved Examples
topics.concept:
Concept Explanations

Modeling (7.1, 7.8). Translate phrases into equations: "rate proportional to amount" → dy/dt = ky; "proportional to the difference from A" → dy/dt = k(y − A); "rate proportional to amount and to room left" → logistic. Watch signs (decay/depreciation ⇒ k < 0).

Verifying solutions (7.2). Substitute the candidate (and its derivatives) into the equation and check it holds. y = Cx² solves x·y' = 2y for every C — the general solution.

Slope fields (7.3). At each point, plot a segment with slope dy/dx. If dy/dx depends only on x, segments in a vertical column are identical; only on y, identical along horizontal rows. Segments are horizontal where dy/dx = 0 (e.g., along y-axis for dy/dx = y). Solution curves flow along the segments.

Separation & IVPs (7.4–7.5). Most AP DE work is separable. After separating and integrating, use the initial point to determine C, then simplify. Example: dy/dx = x/y, y(1) = 1 → y² = x² + C → C = 0 → y = x (the branch through (1,1)).

Growth/decay & logistic (7.6–7.7). Recognize the exponential model instantly and use half-life/doubling relationships. For logistic, remember the population accelerates until M/2, then decelerates toward the carrying capacity.

Worked Examples

Example 1 (Separable). dy/dx = e^(x−y) → e^y dy = e^x dx → e^y = e^x + C.

Example 2 (Separable, harder). x(1 + y²)dx + y(1 + x²)dy = 0 → x/(1+x²)dx + y/(1+y²)dy = 0 → (1/2)ln(1+x²) + (1/2)ln(1+y²) = C₁ → (1 + x²)(1 + y²) = C. (from the GrowQR NCERT/JEE bank)

Example 3 (IVP). dy/dx = 2xy, y(0) = 3 → ln|y| = x² + C₁ → y = Ce^(x²), and y(0) = 3 gives y = 3e^(x²).

Example 4 (Half-life). A substance halves in 10 years: e^(−10k) = 1/2 → k = (ln 2)/10. (from the GrowQR NCERT/JEE bank)

Example 5 (Logistic reasoning). dP/dt = 0.5 P(1 − P/200) grows fastest at P = 100 (= M/2) and levels off near 200.

Example 6 (Slope field to solution). dy/dx = −x/y → y dy = −x dx → x² + y² = C: the solution curves are circles centered at the origin.

quiz.q: For dy/dx = y, where in the slope field are the segments horizontal?
quiz.explanation: Segments are horizontal where dy/dx = 0. Here dy/dx = y = 0 along the x-axis.

quiz.q: A slope field is a graphical representation that shows:
options: short segments whose slopes equal dy/dx at each point
quiz.explanation: A slope field draws a small segment at each point with slope given by the differential equation, suggesting the shape of solution curves.

quiz.q: Solve the separable equation dy/dx = x/y.
quiz.explanation: Separate: y dy = x dx. Integrate: y^2/2 = x^2/2 + C1, so y^2 = x^2 + C.

quiz.q: Solve dy/dx = e^(x - y).
quiz.explanation: Write dy/dx = e^x e^(-y). Separate: e^y dy = e^x dx. Integrate: e^y = e^x + C. (Adapted from the GrowQR NCERT/JEE bank.)

quiz.q: Solve dy/dx = ky (k constant).
quiz.explanation: Separate: dy/y = k dx. Integrate: ln|y| = kx + C1, so y = C e^(kx).

topics.title: Graphical Interpretation, Common Mistakes & Tips
topics.concept:
Graphical Interpretation

  • A slope field is the "flow" of all solution curves; a particular solution threads through the field from its initial point.
  • Exponential growth curves upward ever-faster; decay falls toward 0.
  • The logistic curve is S-shaped (sigmoidal): concave up below M/2, concave down above, with a horizontal asymptote at M.

Common Mistakes

  • Forgetting the constant C (and hence unable to apply the initial condition).
  • Integrating without separating — variables must be fully separated first.
  • Sign errors on decay (k must be negative) and on ∫ dy/y = ln|y|.
  • Logistic mix-ups: fastest growth is at M/2, not at M or at the start.
  • Trying non-AB methods (integrating factors, homogeneous substitutions) on the exam — AB expects separable solutions.

AP Exam Tips

  • Show the separation and the integration step with + C on free-response — both earn points.
  • After finding the general solution, apply the initial condition immediately to get the particular solution.
  • For slope-field items, reason from where dy/dx is 0 or constant.
  • Know the exponential solution y = y₀e^(kt) and half-life/doubling relations without re-deriving them.
  • State logistic facts (equilibria 0 and M; fastest growth at M/2; limit M).

Unit Summary

  • A differential equation models change; separation of variables is the AB solving method.
  • General solution (with C) → apply initial condition → particular solution.
  • Exponential: y = y₀e^(kt); use half-life/doubling to find k.
  • Logistic: equilibria 0 and M, fastest growth at M/2, limit M.
  • Slope fields visualize solution behavior without solving.

Next unit: using integrals for area, volume, average value, and motion.

quiz.q: A radioactive substance decays at a rate proportional to the amount present. If y is the amount, the correct model is:
quiz.explanation: Decay means the amount decreases, so the proportional model has a negative constant: dy/dt = -ky with k > 0.

quiz.q: For which value of r is y = e^(rx) a solution of y'' - 5y' + 6y = 0?
quiz.explanation: Substituting y = e^(rx) gives (r^2 - 5r + 6)e^(rx) = 0, so r^2 - 5r + 6 = (r - 2)(r - 3) = 0, giving r = 2 or r = 3.

quiz.q: A slope field shows segments with slope 0 along the line y = x and positive slopes above it. Which equation could produce it?
quiz.explanation: dy/dx = y - x is 0 when y = x, and positive when y > x (above the line y = x), matching the description.

quiz.q: Solve the separable equation x(1 + y^2) dx + y(1 + x^2) dy = 0.
quiz.explanation: Separate: x/(1+x^2) dx + y/(1+y^2) dy = 0. Integrate: (1/2)ln(1+x^2) + (1/2)ln(1+y^2) = C1, so (1+x^2)(1+y^2) = C. (Adapted from the GrowQR NCERT/JEE bank.)

quiz.q: Solve dy/dx = y with y(0) = 2, and find y(1).
quiz.explanation: The solution is y = C e^x; y(0) = 2 gives C = 2, so y = 2e^x. Then y(1) = 2e.

mock_tests.title: Practice Set A

questions.q: Which of the following is a separable differential equation?
questions.explanation: dy/dx = xy separates as dy/y = x dx. The others cannot be written as a product of a function of x times a function of y.

questions.q: A solution of a differential equation that contains an arbitrary constant is called:
questions.explanation: The general solution includes an arbitrary constant and represents the whole family of solution curves.

questions.q: The order of a differential equation is:
options: the highest derivative that appears in it
questions.explanation: The order is determined by the highest-order derivative present (e.g., dy/dx is first order; d^2y/dx^2 is second order).

questions.q: Solve dy/dx = 6x^2 y.
questions.explanation: Separate: dy/y = 6x^2 dx. Integrate: ln|y| = 2x^3 + C1, so y = C e^(2x^3).

questions.q: Solve the initial-value problem dy/dx = x/y with y(1) = 1. (Take the branch through (1,1).)
questions.explanation: Separating gives y^2 = x^2 + C. Applying y(1) = 1: 1 = 1 + C, so C = 0 and y^2 = x^2. Through (1,1) the solution branch is y = x. (Adapted from the GrowQR NCERT/JEE bank.)

questions.q: Solve dy/dx = 2xy with y(0) = 3.
questions.explanation: Separate: dy/y = 2x dx, so ln|y| = x^2 + C1 and y = C e^(x^2). Using y(0) = 3 gives C = 3, so y = 3 e^(x^2).

questions.q: A particular solution of a differential equation is one that:
options: satisfies a given initial condition (a specific value of C)
questions.explanation: The general solution contains an arbitrary constant; applying an initial condition determines that constant, yielding a particular solution.

questions.q: A substance decays with a half-life of 10 years. The decay constant k in y = y0 e^(-kt) is:
questions.explanation: Half-life: (1/2)y0 = y0 e^(-k*10), so e^(-10k) = 1/2, giving 10k = ln 2 and k = (ln 2)/10. (Adapted from the GrowQR NCERT/JEE bank.)

questions.q: A bacteria culture doubles every 3 hours and follows exponential growth. The growth constant k is:
questions.explanation: Doubling time: 2 y0 = y0 e^(3k), so e^(3k) = 2 and k = (ln 2)/3.

questions.q: If a quantity grows exponentially and triples in 5 years, its value after 10 years (starting from A0) is:
questions.explanation: Tripling every 5 years: after 10 years (two tripling periods) the amount is 3 * 3 = 9 times the initial value, 9 A0.

questions.q: In the logistic model dP/dt = kP(1 - P/M), the constant M represents:
questions.explanation: M is the carrying capacity, the limiting population that the model approaches as t increases.

questions.q: In a logistic model, as t approaches infinity, the population P approaches:
questions.explanation: Logistic solutions level off at the carrying capacity, so P approaches M as t approaches infinity.

questions.q: The velocity of an object under gravity (ignoring air resistance) satisfies dv/dt = -g. If v(0) = v0, then v(t) equals:
questions.explanation: Antidifferentiating dv/dt = -g gives v = -g t + C. Using v(0) = v0 gives C = v0, so v(t) = v0 - g t.

questions.q: Is y = Cx^2 a solution of the differential equation x(dy/dx) = 2y?
questions.explanation: y = Cx^2 gives dy/dx = 2Cx, so x(dy/dx) = 2Cx^2 = 2y. The equation holds for all C, so this is the general solution.

questions.q: Solve dy/dx = 3x^2 with y(1) = 5.
questions.explanation: Antidifferentiate: y = x^3 + C. Using y(1) = 5: 1 + C = 5, so C = 4 and y = x^3 + 4.

questions.q: A colony of bacteria numbers 1000 initially and grows exponentially, reaching 4000 in 2 hours. Its size after 4 hours is:
questions.explanation: It quadruples every 2 hours (1000 -> 4000). After another 2 hours (4 total), it quadruples again: 4000 -> 16000.

questions.q: A logistic population P(t) with carrying capacity 1000 currently has P = 400 and is increasing. As time goes on, P will:
options: keep increasing and level off near 1000
questions.explanation: Below carrying capacity, a logistic population increases and asymptotically approaches the carrying capacity of 1000.

questions.q: Solve dy/dx = y^2 (for y not 0).
questions.explanation: Separate: dy/y^2 = dx. Integrate: -1/y = x + C1, so y = -1/(x + C).

questions.q: Water leaks from a tank so that the volume satisfies dV/dt = -0.2V. This describes:
questions.explanation: dV/dt = -0.2V is the exponential-decay model; the solution is V = V0 e^(-0.2t).

questions.q: For dy/dx = x + y, what is the slope of the solution curve at the point (1, 2)?
questions.explanation: The slope is dy/dx evaluated at the point: 1 + 2 = 3.

mock_tests.title: Practice Set B

questions.q: Which situation is modeled by dy/dt = k (a constant)?
options: a quantity changing at a constant rate
questions.explanation: A constant derivative means the quantity changes at a constant rate, giving a linear function y = kt + C.

questions.q: Solve dy/dx = e^x with y(0) = 3.
questions.explanation: Antidifferentiate: y = e^x + C. Using y(0) = 3: 1 + C = 3, so C = 2 and y = e^x + 2.

questions.q: If dy/dt = 0.05y and y(0) = 200, what is y(t)?
questions.explanation: Exponential growth solution: y = y0 e^(0.05t) = 200 e^(0.05t).

questions.q: Which function is a solution of dy/dx = -2y?
questions.explanation: y = e^(-2x) gives dy/dx = -2 e^(-2x) = -2y, satisfying the equation.

questions.q: Solve dy/dx = (2x)/(y).
questions.explanation: Separate: y dy = 2x dx. Integrate: y^2/2 = x^2 + C1, so y^2 = 2x^2 + C.

questions.q: Newton's Law of Cooling gives dT/dt = -k(T - 20) for an object cooling in a 20-degree room. The equilibrium temperature is:
questions.explanation: Equilibrium occurs where dT/dt = 0: T - 20 = 0, so T = 20 (the object approaches room temperature).

questions.q: The logistic differential equation differs from exponential growth because it includes:
options: a factor that limits growth as P approaches the carrying capacity
questions.explanation: Logistic growth multiplies kP by (1 - P/M), which slows growth as P approaches the carrying capacity M.

questions.q: Solve dy/dx = 4x^3 with y(0) = -1.
questions.explanation: Antidifferentiate: y = x^4 + C. Using y(0) = -1: 0 + C = -1, so y = x^4 - 1.

questions.q: If a quantity decays exponentially to 1/4 of its value in 6 hours, its half-life is:
questions.explanation: Decaying to 1/4 means two successive halvings occurred in 6 hours, so each half-life is 6/2 = 3 hours.

questions.q: In the slope field for dy/dx = 2, every segment has:
questions.explanation: Since dy/dx = 2 is constant, every segment in the slope field is parallel with slope 2 (solutions are lines y = 2x + C).

questions.q: Solve dy/dx = 1/x (x > 0) with y(1) = 0.
questions.explanation: Antidifferentiate: y = ln(x) + C. Using y(1) = 0: ln(1) + C = 0, so C = 0 and y = ln(x).

questions.q: Solve dy/dx = cos(x) with y(0) = 1, then find y(pi/2).
questions.explanation: Antidifferentiate: y = sin(x) + C. y(0) = 1 gives C = 1, so y = sin(x) + 1. Then y(pi/2) = 1 + 1 = 2.

questions.q: A population follows P(t) = 500 e^(0.04t). What is the population growth rate dP/dt when t = 0?
Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5730 years. The decay model uses k equal to:
questions.explanation: From the half-life relation e^(-5730 k) = 1/2, we get k = (ln 2)/5730.

questions.q: For the logistic equation dP/dt = 0.5 P(1 - P/200), the population grows fastest when P equals:
questions.explanation: Logistic growth is fastest at half the carrying capacity, P = M/2 = 200/2 = 100 (this is the inflection point of the solution curve).

questions.q: For dP/dt = kP(1 - P/M), the equilibrium solutions (where dP/dt = 0) are:
questions.explanation: dP/dt = 0 when P = 0 or when 1 - P/M = 0, i.e., P = M. These are the two equilibrium (constant) solutions.

questions.q: A tank holds 100 L of pure water. Brine with 2 g/L of salt flows in at 5 L/min (and well-mixed solution flows out at 5 L/min). If S is the salt amount, the model for dS/dt is:
questions.explanation: Salt in = (2 g/L)(5 L/min) = 10 g/min. Salt out = (concentration S/100)(5 L/min) = 5S/100. So dS/dt = 10 - 5S/100. (Mixing model adapted from the GrowQR JEE bank.)

questions.q: A savings account grows continuously at 4% per year: dA/dt = 0.04A. If A(0) = 1000, the balance after t years is:
questions.explanation: Continuous growth dA/dt = 0.04A has solution A = A0 e^(0.04t). With A0 = 1000, A(t) = 1000 e^(0.04t).

questions.q: Solve dy/dx = (y ln y)/x with the solution curve passing through (1, e).
questions.explanation: Separate: dy/(y ln y) = dx/x. Let u = ln y; du = dy/y. Then du/u = dx/x, so ln|ln y| = ln|x| + C1, giving ln y = Cx. Through (1, e): ln e = C(1), so C = 1 and ln y = x, i.e., y = e^x. (Adapted from the GrowQR JEE bank.)

questions.q: For the slope field of dy/dx = -x/y, the solution curves are:
questions.explanation: Separating dy/dx = -x/y gives y dy = -x dx, so y^2/2 = -x^2/2 + C, i.e., x^2 + y^2 = C: circles centered at the origin.
